description: ODC (EDIT and REFACTORING coverage of EXPOSED REST): touch an endpoint that THIS job did not create. The base is job:rest-expose, that is, the IRestService WfCovZoneService, the method WfCovGetZone (GET /WfCovGetZone/{Postcode}) and the shareable structure WfCovZoneInfo already exist when the first op runs - there is not a single creation op of the service here, on purpose, because creating and editing in the same job proves no maintenance at all. The four changes are all on top of what the other job left written: add a method to the inherited service (reusing the inherited structure as the type of the output), change the HTTPMethod of a method that already existed, rename that method and rename the service itself. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: the service is cited as 'IRestService:WfCovZoneService' and a method by the path 'IRestService:WfCovZoneService/WfCovGetZone'. The POINT of the job is the proof read in ops 12 to 14: renaming an exposed REST method REWRITES the URLPath on its own - the segment with the method name changes, and with it the public URL - while the rename returns consumers 0 and expressionsRewritten 0, because the model does not see, and cannot see, the external consumer that is left knocking on a door that no longer exists. Whoever trusts the counter delivers a changed endpoint thinking nothing was touched. The job closes the lesson with the two counter-proofs: after the URLPath is written BY HAND without the method name in it (op 15), a SECOND rename no longer touches it (op 17); and renaming the SERVICE touches the other half of the same URL - BaseURL and URL - without touching the URLPath of any method (ops 20 to 23).

ops.name: WfCovZoneService
ops._why: (0) THE STARTING POINT IS INHERITED: nothing here was created by this job. The service, the method and the structure come from job:rest-expose, and the find proves it before the first write op runs.

(1) BEFORE, the service: Actions 1, the Description that the OTHER job wrote, and the two halves of the public URL that matter to the rest of the job - BaseURL /rest/WfCovZoneService (derived from the NAME of the service) and URL /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneService.
(2) BEFORE, the whole inherited tree: one method, the input Postcode, the output Info and the three nodes of the flow. This is the snapshot the dump (24) is compared with.

(3) BEFORE, the inherited method: HTTPMethod GET, URLPath /WfCovGetZone/{Postcode} and the full URL /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneService/WfCovGetZone/{Postcode}. Note the composition, because it explains everything that follows: the public URL is BaseURL (name of the SERVICE) + URLPath (which is born from the name of the METHOD).

(4) BEFORE, the inherited data contract: the Public structure (in ODC vocabulary, shareable) that types the output of the inherited method. The new method of change 1 reuses it instead of declaring another - it is what distinguishes adding a method to an existing service from making a new service next to it.

ops.name: WfCovRateZone
ops._why: (5a) CHANGE 1 - add a method to the INHERITED service. The parent is not an $alias: aliases are local to the job that declares them, and another job declared this service; outside it the stable reference is 'IRestService:WfCovZoneService'. The Wf prefix is because it is a NEW element.

(5b) WHAT THE PLATFORM GIVES FOR FREE, and it is the root of all the danger in this job: the method is born already with Nodes 2 (Start and End, which is why they are never created by hand), HTTPMethod GET and - the point - URLPath '/WfCovRateZone', DERIVED FROM THE NAME. Nobody wrote that URLPath. And because it is born from the name, the rename in op (12) rewrites it.

ops.value: Classifica uma zona. Acrescentado por rest-expose-lifecycle.json ao servico que job:rest-expose criou.
ops._why: The Description of a REST method is author text, and it is also a WATCHED write: the data contract now checks named top-level elements, and IRestServiceAction is one of them. If this write did not stick, the job failed with 'Data property mismatch' even with a clean Verify.
the INHERITED structure, read in op (4), typing the output of the new method: the exposed contract of the service is still a single one.
the Start and the End are the ones the method brought from op (5b); only what goes in the middle is missing.

(5c) AFTER: InputParameters 1, OutputParameters 1, Nodes 3, POST, and the full URL /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneService/WfCovRateZone - built on the INHERITED BaseURL. A new method enters under the address that already existed.
(5d) AFTER, the service: Actions went from 1 to 2 and nothing else changed - compare with get (1). Adding a method does not rewrite the service.
(6) BEFORE change 2, the inherited method again, so the pair of reads sits next to the change: GET, /WfCovGetZone/{Postcode}.

(7a) CHANGE 2 - the HTTPMethod of a method that ALREADY EXISTED. Changing the verb of a published endpoint is a contract break for whoever consumes it, and in the model it is a set of a single property: no Verify message is born from it (the 55 are still those of the fixture). The platform has no way of knowing who was calling on GET.
(7b) AFTER: the HTTPMethod CHANGED (GET -> POST); the URLPath and the URL STAYED, byte for byte. Changing the verb does not touch the address - it is the separation that op (12) will break.

ops.value: API de zonas de cheia. O metodo WfCovGetZone responde em /rest/WfCovZoneService/WfCovGetZone/{Postcode}.
ops._why: (8) DELIBERATE write of author text that cites the name of the service AND the name of the method AND the URL - all three to be renamed or rewritten next. It stays here so that get (21) shows what the rename does NOT follow. Description is text; a URL inside text is just text.

(9) BEFORE the rename, and it is the most important reading of the whole job: count 0, real 0. The method is exposed to the world and the model knows NO consumer of it, because whoever consumes it is outside the module, outside the tenant, outside the platform. That is why nothing and nobody can warn about what op (12) is going to do.

ops.name: WfCovZoneLookup
ops._why: (10) CHANGE 3 - rename the INHERITED method. The result returns consumers 0 and expressionsRewritten 0: by the counter, nothing happened. Read the next op before believing it.

(11) THE CENTRAL PROOF, and it is what this job exists to show: the URLPath went from /WfCovGetZone/{Postcode} to /WfCovZoneLookup/{Postcode} ON ITS OWN, and the public URL with it - /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneService/WfCovZoneLookup/{Postcode}. No op wrote URLPath. The platform rewrote the SEGMENT that was equal to the old name, for the same reason op (5b) showed: the URLPath is born from the name. A rename that the counter reported as harmless changed the public door of the endpoint, and every external consumer started getting 404. Always compare by the get, never by the number.

(12a) CHANGE 4 - the URLPath of a method that ALREADY EXISTED, written BY HAND over what the platform derived. It is two things at once: the address change the job asked for (from the inherited /WfCovGetZone/{Postcode} to a path by resource) and the FIX of the trap of op (11) - from here on the address is an author decision, not a side effect of the name. The ORDER here is mandatory: this set AFTER the rename. In the opposite order - set and then rename - the data contract fails the job, measured: 'Data property mismatch: {"property":"URLPath","expected":"/WfCovGetZone/{Postcode}/lookup","actual":"/WfCovZoneLookup/{Postcode}/lookup"}'. It is not a defect of the contract: it is the contract catching, with a clean Verify, exactly the write that the rename undid behind the author's back.
(12b) AFTER: URLPath /zones/{Postcode} and URL /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneService/zones/{Postcode}. The name of the method no longer appears in the address.

ops.name: WfCovZoneRead
ops._why: (13) COUNTER-PROOF 1 - the same rename, on the same method, again. If the platform rewrote the URLPath because it is a rename, it would rewrite it now too.

(13b) and it did NOT rewrite: URLPath is still /zones/{Postcode}, letter for letter, with the method already called WfCovZoneRead. It closes the lesson of op (11): what the platform rewrites is the SEGMENT equal to the old name, not the path. A hand-written URLPath, without the name of the method in it, is immune to the rename - and it is the only way for a published endpoint to survive a refactoring of names.
(14) BEFORE change 5: BaseURL /rest/WfCovZoneService and URL /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneService, still with the inherited name.

ops.name: WfCovZoneApi
ops._why: (15) CHANGE 5 - rename the inherited SERVICE itself. Again consumers 0 and expressionsRewritten 0.

(16) AFTER: BaseURL and URL changed on their own to /rest/WfCovZoneApi and /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneApi - the same silent rewrite as in op (11), on the OTHER half of the URL. AND READ BACK WHAT WAS LEFT BEHIND: the Description written in op (8) still says WfCovZoneService, WfCovGetZone and the whole old URL - three names that no longer exist. Author text never follows; only the hand corrects it, and this job leaves it on purpose, so the difference stays visible.

(17) The inherited method seen after the rename of the service: the full URL was dragged to /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneApi/zones/{Postcode}, but the URLPath is still /zones/{Postcode}. COUNTER-PROOF 2: renaming the service touches the BaseURL, renaming the method touches the URLPath; they are different halves of the same public URL, and neither of the two operations warns.

(18) and the NEW method was dragged by the same BaseURL, to /InsuranceApp/rest/WfCovZoneApi/WfCovRateZone, without anything being written to it after op (5c). The alias $novo still resolves because THIS job created it - the difference between what is inherited and what is added.

ops.name: WfCovGetZone
ops._why: (19) empty list: the inherited name disappeared from the module. Only the text of the Description still cites it, and text is not model.

(20) The final tree, set next to dump (2): the service has another name, the two methods (the inherited one renamed and the new one, which enters at the END), the inherited method keeps the input Postcode, the output Info and its three nodes - renaming and changing the address recreates no flow at all -, and the new method brings its own Start, Assign and End. Two name changes, two address changes, one more method, and zero rebuilding underneath: this is what a maintenance job has to be able to show.
